Compute Tajima's D with block jackknife standard errors

Source: R/jackknife_pop_tajimas_d.R
jackknife_pop_tajimas_d.Rd

This function computes genome-wide Tajima's D, together with its standard error estimated with a weighted block jackknife.

Usage

jackknife_pop_tajimas_d(
  .x,
  type = c("matrix", "tidy", "list"),
  block_size,
  size_unit = c("snp", "cM", "bp")
)

Arguments

.x

a gen_tibble object, optionally grouped by one variable

type

type of object to return, if using grouped method. One of "matrix", "tidy", or "list". Default is "matrix".

block_size

The size of the blocks to leave out.

size_unit

Either "snp", "cM" or "bp". If "snp", the block size is in number of SNPs. If "cM", the block size is in centiMorgans. If "bp", the block size is in base pairs.

Value

if data is not grouped, a data frame with the following columns:

  • estimate: Tajima's D computed on all loci

  • jack_estimate: the bias corrected jackknife estimate

  • se: the jackknife standard error

  • z: the z score (jack_estimate/se)

  • n_blocks: the number of blocks used if data are grouped, either: a data frame with the following columns:

  • quantity: the quantity reported in the row (estimate, jack_estimate, se, z or n_blocks, as described above)

  • group: the value of the quantity for the group (there will be as many of these columns as groups in the gen_tibble, and they will be named by the grouping levels) a tidy tibble with the following columns:

  • group: the name of the group

  • estimate, jack_estimate, se, z, n_blocks: as described above or a list of data frames, one per group, with the same columns as for ungrouped data.

Details

The genome is divided into non-overlapping blocks, which never span more than one chromosome, and Tajima's D is recomputed leaving out one block at a time. The standard error is computed with the weighted delete-m jackknife of Busing et al. (1999), where each block is weighted by the number of loci it contains. Tajima's D is a function of sums across loci (of the nucleotide diversity, the number of segregating sites, and quantities that depend on the sample size of each locus), so leaving out a block is achieved by subtracting its sums, without having to rescan the genotypes. See jackknife_stats_generic() for details.

Missing genotypes are accounted for by using the number of non-missing allele copies at each locus as its sample size, following Bailey et al. (2025) as implemented in pixy. See pop_tajimas_d() for details. Loci with no genotyped individuals are ignored.

References

Busing FMTA, Meijer E, Van Der Leeden R (1999) Delete-m jackknife for unequal m. Statistics and Computing 9:3-8.

Bailey N, Stevison L, Samuk K (2025) Correcting for bias in estimates of \(\theta_W\) and Tajima's D from missing data in next-generation sequencing. Molecular Ecology Resources, e14104. doi:10.1111/1755-0998.14104

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

# Calculate Tajima's D using blocks of 2 SNPs
example_gt %>%
  jackknife_pop_tajimas_d(
    block_size = 2,
    size_unit = "snp"
  )
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   quantity       pop1     pop2  pop3
#>   <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 estimate      0.944  -0.780   -Inf
#> 2 jack_estimate 1.04   -0.861     NA
#> 3 se            0.329   0.0297    NA
#> 4 z             3.14  -29.0       NA
#> 5 n_blocks      3       3          3
